title: Regulated Customer Go‑Live & Security Gate Playbook
author: Asha Menon
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook documents the go‑live gating criteria, runbook steps, and operational handoff for regulated enterprise customers (examples: finance, healthcare, govt). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Security, SRE, and the customer’s technical contacts. The goal is to ensure a predictable, auditable, and secure path to production that satisfies common regulatory demands: data residency, encryption, audit logging, and least privilege.

Summary of purpose:
- Standardize go‑live gates for regulated customers.
- Provide a reproducible checklist owners can run prior to final cutover.
- Define rollback criteria and escalation paths if post‑go‑live thresholds are violated.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where the customer requires regulatory controls beyond our standard onboarding. Not for internal prototype or POC environments.

Key owners and contacts
-----------------------
- CS Lead / Primary: Asha Menon (Customer Success) — final go/no‑go authority for commercial readiness.
- Security Reviewer: Priya Desai (Security) — approves encryption, KMS, and audit log configuration.
- SRE Lead: Marco Alvarez (SRE) — validates network, capacity, and monitoring.
- Integration Engineer (Redwood): assigned per account.
- Customer Technical Lead: named in the account record.

Preconditions (must be completed before Gate 1)
-----------------------------------------------
1) Contract & Data Processing Addendum signed and counter‑signed.
2) Customer identity and account provisioning completed in Okta / Redwood IAM.
3) Initial traffic shaping and capacity reservation (Dedicated or Private) configured in billing and infra.
4) Customer provides IP allowlists and required subnets for VPC peering if applicable.
5) CS and Security have a documented list of regulated data types and retention requirements.

Gate definitions and acceptance criteria
---------------------------------------
Gate 0: Legal & Commercial (CS) — signoff required by CS and Legal
- DPA executed and stored in contracting system (Yes/No).
- Billing terms and reserved capacity committed (Yes/No).
Owner: CS.

Gate 1: Identity, Access, and Keying (Security) — must pass before any customer data flows
- Customer account created and 2FA enforced for all Redwood console users.
- RBAC roles configured (roles: admin, ops, audit‑viewer).
- Customer KMS configured and integrated (KMS key ID: provided).
- Secrets rotation policy scheduled (30/60/90 days).
Owner: Security.

Gate 2: Network & Data Residency (SRE/Security)
- VPC peering or private link validated (latency < 25 ms, packet loss < 0.1%).
- Egress/ingress firewall rules validated (ports: 443, 9443 for private).
- Data store region confirmed and data residency tests executed (sample write/read check).
Owner: SRE.

Gate 3: Observability, Auditability & Monitoring (SRE/Product)
- Audit logging enabled: all API token events, admin actions, and model version changes stream to audit S3 bucket and SIEM.
- Log retention policy matches contract (e.g., 7 years for finance customers).
- Dashboards created: Token cost by route, P95 latency by model, error budget burn rate.
- Alerting: page to oncall when error rate > 0.1% (5m window) or P95 latency > 500ms (10m window).
Owner: SRE/Product.

Gate 4: Quality & Acceptance (CS/Product)
- Customer test set executed with no major regressions (>98% of prompts within expected response class).
- Throughput test: sustained RPS for 1 hour at expected commit level with <1% 5xxs.
- Canary traffic run for 24 hours with progressive ramp.
Owner: Product/CS.

Gate 5: Final Go‑Live (CS/Customer)
- Customer signoff recorded in the ticketing system.
- Cutover window scheduled and comms templates sent.
- Post‑go‑live monitoring playbook acknowledged.
Owner: CS (coordinated with Customer).

Pre‑Go‑Live checklist (operational items)
----------------------------------------
- [ ] Ticket created: "Regulated Go‑Live - <customer>" with all attachments.
- [ ] Assigned SRE, CS, Security, and IntegrationEngineer.
- [ ] Backup snapshots and recovery point objectives verified.
- [ ] KMS audit logs accessible to customer if contractually required.
- [ ] Rate limits and quotas configured per contract (requests/min, tokens/day).
- [ ] Prometheus metrics endpoint verified and dashboard IDs placed in ticket.
- [ ] Canaries deployed for at least two production regions if multi‑region required.

Example validation commands and checks
------------------------------------
1) Verify audit log ship:
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_AUDIT_KEY" 
     https://audit-api.redwood.example.com/v1/events?limit=5 | jq '.[0:5]'

2) KMS integration smoke test (example using AWS KMS):
   aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE \
     --plaintext "test" --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode || echo "KMS test failed"

3) Data residency read/write check (pseudo):
   # write a small object and confirm it lands in the correct region bucket
   aws s3 cp testfile s3://redwood-audit-<customer>-us-east-1/testfile --region us-east-1

Operational SLOs and thresholds (customer-facing)
--------------------------------------------------
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated.
- Latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 240ms for generation endpoints (standard model profile).
- Error rate: 5xx < 0.1% over rolling 1 hour.
- Audit delivery: 100% of admin events shipped within 5 minutes to SIEM.

Rollback criteria (post‑go‑live)
-------------------------------
Initiate rollback if any of the following occur during the first 48 hours after cutover:
1) Sustained error rate > 1% for 15 minutes.
2) P95 latency > 2x committed latency for 30 minutes.
3) Data residency breach confirmed (any object written to unapproved region).
4) Customer reports reproducible data corruption or missing audit events.

Rollback steps (high level)
1) Invoke immediate traffic diversion back to pre‑production or fallback model variant.
2) Notify all owners and open an incident ticket (severity P1).
3) Revoke any temporary credentials provisioned during cutover.
4) Restore from snapshot if data integrity compromised.

Escalation matrix (who to call)
--------------------------------
- 0‑15 minutes: Oncall SRE (pager) + CS primary via Slack @channel.
- 15‑60 minutes: Escalate to SRE Lead Marco Alvarez and Security Reviewer Priya Desai.
- >60 minutes or regulatory breach: Exec notification to VP CS and VP Security; schedule stakeholder war room.

Communications and customer-facing artifacts
-------------------------------------------
- Pre‑cutover email (template): short summary of cutover, expected downtime (if any), contact list, and rollback window.
- Post‑cutover report: performance summary, audit event snapshot, incident notes (if any).
- Ticket template fields required: impact, rollback_criteria, monitoring_links, affected_regions, customer_signoff.

QBR and health check metrics to track for first 90 days
-----------------------------------------------------
- M0 (Day 7): Activation health: success rate of customer API key calls, first‑hour error rate, top 5 error signatures.
- M1 (Day 30): Cost and latency report vs committed SLA; KV cache hit rate and effective token cost reduction.
- M3 (Day 90): Reliability report: uptime, incident summary, and security audit summary.

Template: Post‑Go‑Live Health Snapshot (to attach to QBR)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Uptime (30d): 99.xx%
- Average P95 latency (30d): NNNms
- Error budget burn (30d): N tokens / %
- Audit events ingested (30d): NNNNN
- Cost per 1k tokens vs baseline: $X.XX

Appendix: Common regulatory workarounds and mitigations
------------------------------------------------------
- If customer requires on‑prem KMS and Redwood hosted control plane, implement envelope encryption (customer key wraps Redwood master key) and document key access agreements.
- For customers with strict egress policies, use dedicated private link endpoints and deploy a regional-only control plane where possible.
- Where log retention exceeds standard retention, forward a copy to customer‑managed S3 with lifecycle rules; redact PII at ingestion step.

Audit artifacts to provide to customer (examples)
------------------------------------------------
- Deployment architecture diagram (PDF).
- RBAC role list and last 90 days of admin actions (CSV).
- KMS key ARNs and rotation schedule (CSV).
- Penetration test summary (redacted) and SOC2 attestation link.
